issues.title: Higher FOV and resolution for Panini projection
issues.body: I wanted to test whether the Panini projection option fixes https://mojira.dev/MC-127400 . So far it looks promising, but now there are three new reasons for headaches: 1. The FOV becomes very zoomed in. Maximum FOV looks more like the middle setting of the FOV slider. This way, of course I don't see the issues that large FOV values in Minecraft have, because I can't have a large FOV anymore. 🙃 2. The middle of the screen becomes very blurry. With maximum FOV, Speed 2, Soul speed 3, sprinting and full FOV effects, I can barely see what I'm running towards here: I'm sure it's fine, though. ;) And the village house in the background looks even worse… except it's not even a house, it's a well! 85×60 pixels should be enough to differentiate that, but what I see is more like 5×4 pixels. This was also mentioned in https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra/issues/596#issuecomment-5557298482. Rendering at 15× resolution would fix that completely, but also cause a lot of lag. So maybe a configurable resolution multiplier? Or maybe it could render only the center at higher resolution. 3. At least in my quick test now, it seemed potentially more laggy than without the option, which seems reasonable, but might also be because of the million other things that my laptop was doing at the same time. Maybe there would be a way to implement this feature as a single render pass instead of modifying the image afterwards, which would fix #2 and #3. But that's probably a lot of effort and not worth it during the experimental phase.

issues.title: Add Simplified Chinese (zh_cn) translation for Minecraft 26.3
issues.body:
Hi, and thanks for the great mod!

This adds a complete **Simplified Chinese (`zh_cn`)** translation for the Minecraft **26.3** Fabric version. The file `zh_cn.json` is attached below.

Details:
- Manually reviewed (with light AI assistance).
- I release this contribution under **CC0**, so you may ship it under your project's own license.
- Happy to adjust any terminology. Thank you!

issues.title: [Feature Request] Add option to remove environmental and rain fog specifically (pre-26.2)
issues.body:
EDIT: I realized this is a duplicate of https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra/issues/460. However, Sodium Extra 0.9.3 for 26.1.2 does not seem to have advanced fog settings for environmental and rain fog. https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra/issues/460#issuecomment-4827664948 states that these changes were applied to the 26.2 branch, not any of the previous versions. Therefore, I believe these qualify as missing controls from the old fog system.

It would be great to have separate options for disabling environmental fog and rain fog without having to disable all overworld fog.

This would give players more control over the atmospheric visibility, especially for those who want to remove certain environmental effects while keeping the main fog (the one that hides chunks) enabled.

It would be neat if these new settings worked regardless of fog shape (cylindrical, planar, etc)

issues.title: [Feature Request] Extended Max Framerate slider limit and custom cap override
issues.body:
**Description**
With high-refresh-rate monitors becoming more and more common, the vanilla 250 FPS limit on the frame rate slider forces players with high refresh rate monitors to go straight into the "Unlimited" setting. It would be a good QoL feature to extend the vanilla Max Framerate slider to support higher frame rate caps and finer step adjustments, and arbitrary higher limits.

**My suggestion** 
- Change the slider increment step from vanilla's 10 FPS to 5 FPS for more precise settings like 165,175,185 FPS
- Provide an option to allow players to set an exact target beyond vanilla's limit of 250 FPS (e.g., capping precisely at 310 FPS).

issues.title: Feature Request: More options for using half resolution in fullscreen mode
issues.body:
Hi, I am playing Minecraft on a MacBook Pro with the Retina display. Therefore, I sometimes want to use the feature where the game runs at half resolution in full screen mode. The problem is that I don't want to use half resolution every time I am in fullscreen mode.

Because macOS has two different full screen modes (Minecraft fullscreen mode when pressing f11 and macOS native fullscreen mode when pressing fn+f), I would suggest the following feature:

 - When Minecraft is using the f11 borderless fullscreen mode, the game runs at half resolution
 - When Minecraft is in the macOS native fullscreen mode, the game runs at full resolution

In addition, is there a way that the GUI size then will always stay the same, so GUI elements don't look smaller when using a higher resolution. Thank you in advance.

issues.title: Feature request: Only reduce resolution under macOS when using Minecraft fullscreen mode (f11) - not when using native macOS fullscreen mode (fn+f)
Feature Request: Automatically adjust GUI scale when changing fullscreen render resolution (macOS)
issues.body:
When using the Sodium Extra option to reduce the fullscreen render resolution on macOS, the physical size of the Minecraft GUI changes because the resolution changes when using f11 Minecraft fullscreen mode.

Currently, switching between native fullscreen resolution and half resolution requires manually changing the Minecraft GUI Scale every time to keep the interface the same visual size. (e. g. when you want to use your game in the macOS native fullscreen mode with fn + f at full resolution: gui size is fine - when using fullscreen with f11 at half resolution, gui is too big for that resolution.)

It would be great if Sodium Extra could offer an option such as:
Automatically adjust GUI scale to maintain consistent on-screen size when fullscreen render resolution changes.

Example:

* Native fullscreen resolution → GUI Scale: 4x
* Half fullscreen resolution → automatically use 2x

The result would be that menus, hotbar, inventory, and other GUI elements appear the same physical size on screen, regardless of the selected fullscreen render resolution.

This would make switching between performance mode (half resolution) and quality mode (native resolution) seamless, without requiring manual GUI adjustments each time.

issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

0.8.7 / 0.9.1 Fabric

### Sodium version.

0.8.12 / 0.9.1beta2 Fabric

### What happened?

Mod Menu reports that an update for Sodium Extra is available when Sodium 0.8.12 and Sodium Extra 0.8.7 are installed.

Sodium currently has two active versions, 0.8.12 and 0.9.1-beta-2. Since both are active, _Mod Menu does not report that Sodium itself has an update available_ because some people may wish to remain on the stable version rather than use the beta. (I assume this allowing of both versions is done by Sodium either on Modrinth or within the mods themselves.)

However, to clear the fact that a Sodium Extra update is available, one must install Sodium Extra 0.9.1, which then causes the Fabric loader to crash and give the cure as installing Sodium 0.9.1 beta 2, which the user may not want to do.

Yes, the solution could be "user should ignore the fact an update is available", which I will do for the time being, but if Sodium can somehow suppress the fact there is an update available, Sodium Extra might also be able to do the same, and not force people down the path of having to install a Sodium beta.

Finding the 0.8.7 version to downgrade back to is not quite as easy as installing the latest version on Modrinth.

This might not be something that can be fixed this time for the current and previous versions, but it might be something that can be done for later releases.

issues.title: Linux & Fullscreen Resolution
issues.body:
You've had this issue before, I'm aware, but hear me out.

As you know this has been disabled for Linux users in recent versions, and from what I can tell you cite Wayland and it's... just so brilliant implementations as the issue; support for exclusive fullscreen is very much dependent on what compositor you use, I get that.

However, for people like me, who do use Wayland, and know for a fact that their compositor does handle this correctly (in my case, that'd be Kwin) as they've used this option in previous versions, this is a rather annoying "fix"; as now I'm trying to render a game comprised of pixel art and cubes in 4K, leading to extreme thermals, poor performance, and me no longer being able to listen to music or watch a YouTube video in the background while playing Minecraft in fullscreen.

Yes, my hardware is... limited. However the fact of the matter is that, like I said, this used to work flawlessly, and now doesn't due to artificial limitations.

A better solution in my eyes would be to inform users on Linux that support is "experimental" or "unstable", and that the user experience can vary between DEs/WMs (yes the technical term is compositor on Wayland but most people know DE and WM). If it causes the game to crash or not render correctly or whatever, then so be it, the user can find a way around that if needs be (such as editing their options outside the game or reinstalling their instance).

Point that I'm trying to make is this, you're in the right mindset to put UX first, but artificial limitations never did anyone any good, and what you're protecting against is ultimately reversible shall the need arise.

That's all, thank your for your efforts on this project so far. <3

issues.title: Compatibility with modern Sodium 0.8.12 alpha backports to 1.21.1
issues.body:
Hi,
I'm a maintainer on Sodium and today we published the first alpha from our graduated backport experiment. This means that we [now have Sodium 0.8.12 on 1.21.1](https://modrinth.com/mod/sodium/versions?c=alpha&g=1.21.1). You can find more information about this [in our blog post on discord](https://discord.com/channels/602796788608401408/1077645005042233374/1501010160326414426).

We've since noticed Sodium Extra interacting with Sodium and not working properly. In particular the Sodium Extra options don't appear on our settings screen, and while I have not observed crashes I wouldn't count on there being none. The gist is that since 0.8.x includes many changes to various parts of Sodium, including our new Config API, mods such as Sable or this one, will encounter breakage when users (cluelessly) update modpacks with the latest published versions.

If you'd like to coordinate more closely with us, you're invited to [our discord server.](https://caffeinemc.net/discord) I intend for this to be considered a "feature" since this software is currently in alpha and not the mainline release. A lack of compatibility is not a fault on your part, but rather I would just like to notify you of the situation. I hope this doesn't cause too much trouble!

Thanks!

issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [x] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Minecraft version.

1.21.11

### Sodium Extra version.

0.8.3

### Sodium version.

0.8.7

### What happened?

This took me a while to track down, especially because the error sounds weird… When a resource pack is active in which `subtitles.entity.generic.splash` is replaced with an empty or semi-empty string (so `""` or `" "`, but not `"a"`), the game crashes on launch. This does not happen with a bunch of other strings and does not even require that subtitle to be shown or any world to even be opened.
Here is a minimalistic `.minecraft` folder to reproduce the issue: [minecraft.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26633302/minecraft.zip)
Add [`sodium-extra-fabric-0.8.3+mc1.21.11.jar`](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra/releases/download/mc26.1.1-0.8.7/sodium-extra-fabric-0.8.7+mc26.1.1.jar) and [`sodium-fabric-0.8.7+mc1.21.11.jar`](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/AANobbMI/versions/UddlN6L4/sodium-fabric-0.8.7%2Bmc1.21.11.jar) to the "`mods`" folder.

### Relevant log.

https://mclo.gs/LbLbcNB

### Additional information.

Error:
```
Description: Mod 'sodium-extra' failed while registering config options.
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Name must not be blank
```

issues.title: light_updates_warning should default to inOverlay instead of alwaysOn
issues.body:
## Problem

When `light_updates_warning` is set to `alwaysOn` in `debug-profile.json` (which happens after migrating config from a previous MC version), it triggers `DebugScreenOverlay.extractRenderState()` to call `graphics.nextStratum()` every frame — even though the entry produces no visible output (because `renderSettings.lightUpdates` defaults to `true`, so the condition in `display()` is never met).

This creates empty render strata in MC 26.1's new `GuiRenderState` system, which corrupts the z-ordering of other GUI elements. In practice, this makes malilib/MiniHUD's HUD text completely invisible.

## Root Cause

In `SodiumExtraClientMod.init()`:
```java
defaultProfile.put(lightUpdatesWarning, DebugScreenEntryStatus.ALWAYS_ON);
```

This causes the entry to persist as `alwaysOn` in `debug-profile.json`. After version migration, the entry stays `alwaysOn` even in a fresh install of Sodium Extra.

## Suggested Fix

Use `IN_OVERLAY` instead of `ALWAYS_ON`:
```java
defaultProfile.put(lightUpdatesWarning, DebugScreenEntryStatus.IN_OVERLAY);
```

This way the entry only renders when F3 overlay is active, avoiding the empty strata issue during normal gameplay.

## Environment

- Minecraft 26.1.1
- Sodium 0.8.9
- Sodium Extra 0.8.6
- MiniHUD 0.39.1 / MaLiLib 0.28.2

Note: I've also reported the underlying MC bug (empty `nextStratum()` calls in `DebugScreenOverlay`) to Mojang, but changing the default status on your side is a much faster fix.

issues.title: Armour Durability HUD not showing when Sodium Extra is enabled
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [x] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Minecraft version.

26.1

### Sodium Extra version.

0.8.6

### Sodium version.

0.8.9

### What happened?

When I enable Sodium Extra, my mod Armour Durability HUD stops working. The HUD no longer appears on the screen.

If I disable Sodium Extra, the Armour Durability HUD works normally again.

Steps to Reproduce:

Install Sodium Extra and Armour Durability HUD
Launch the game with both mods enabled
Join a world
Notice that the armour durability HUD is not visible

Expected Behavior:
The armour durability HUD should be visible even when Sodium Extra is enabled.

Actual Behavior:
The HUD does not show at all when Sodium Extra is enabled.

Environment:

Minecraft Version: 26.1
Mod Loader: Fabric
Sodium Extra Version: All version with 26.1+
Armour Durability HUD Version: 26.1+

Additional Info:
No crashes occur — the HUD simply does not render.

issues.title: Crash on startup due to invalid ResourceLocation path (non-ASCII character) in Sodium Extra config
issues.body:
Minecraft crashes during startup when Sodium Extra tries to register config options.
The crash is caused by an invalid ResourceLocation path containing a non-ASCII character (ı, Turkish dotless i).

Error message:

Non [a-z0-9/._-] character in path of location:
sodium-extra:atmospherıc_environment_start


This happens because fogType.name().toLowerCase() is locale-dependent.
On systems using the Turkish locale, toLowerCase() converts I → ı instead of i, which produces an invalid resource path.

Stacktrace (relevant part)
at me.flashyreese.mods.sodiumextra.client.config.SodiumExtraConfig.id(SodiumExtraConfig.java:28)
at me.flashyreese.mods.sodiumextra.client.config.SodiumExtraConfig.createRenderPage(SodiumExtraConfig.java:314)

Affected Code (original)

File: SodiumExtraConfig.java
Method: createRenderPage(...)

IntegerOptionBuilder envEnd = builder.createIntegerOption(
    id(fogType.name().toLowerCase() + "_environment_end")
)
.setEnabled(((Option) SodiumExtraClientMod.mixinConfig()
    .getOptions().get("mixin.fog")).isEnabled())
.setName((class_2561) class_2561.method_43469(
    "sodium-extra.option.fog_type.environment_end",
    new Object[] { fogTypeName(fogType) }
))
.setTooltip((class_2561) class_2561.method_43471(
    "sodium-extra.option.fog_type.environment_end.tooltip"
))
.setStorageHandler(SodiumExtraClientMod.options())
.setRange(0, 300, 1)
.setValueFormatter(ControlValueFormatterImpls.percentage())
.setDefaultValue(100)
.setBinding((), ());

Fix / Workaround

Force a locale-independent lowercase conversion using Locale.ROOT.

Fixed Code
import java.util.Locale;

IntegerOptionBuilder envEnd = builder.createIntegerOption(
    id(fogType.name().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) + "_environment_end")
)
.setEnabled(((Option) SodiumExtraClientMod.mixinConfig()
    .getOptions().get("mixin.fog")).isEnabled())
.setName((class_2561) class_2561.method_43469(
    "sodium-extra.option.fog_type.environment_end",
    new Object[] { fogTypeName(fogType) }
))
.setTooltip((class_2561) class_2561.method_43471(
    "sodium-extra.option.fog_type.environment_end.tooltip"
))
.setStorageHandler(SodiumExtraClientMod.options())
.setRange(0, 300, 1)
.setValueFormatter(ControlValueFormatterImpls.percentage())
.setDefaultValue(100)
.setBinding((), ());

Additional Notes:
This issue only occurs on systems using the Turkish locale,
The same fix may be required anywhere name().toLowerCase() is used for ResourceLocation IDs
Using Locale.ROOT is the standard and safe solution

issues.title: Request Sharp Biome Borders
issues.body:
Minecraft is a blocky game.  While many (crazy people) seem to want to change that and make it less and less blocky, I like the blockiness and wish to embrace it.  I _want_ sharp boarders between my biomes, so it's clear when I'm stepping from one to the other!  I mean, it's not like the color blending also extend to the actual biome boarders themselves, they're still just as sharp as ever, it's just not as easy to see that difference.  But as that sharp difference does, in fact, exist, and can matter (like fishing loot tables, etc.), I like to be able to know and see the difference in game.


Can you please let me turn biome blending off completely (like I used to be able to do)?!?  Thanks!!!

issues.title: [Feedback] Sodium Extra 0.6.6 – New Fog Render Settings
issues.body:
First of all, I'd like to specify that I don't code or anything, so sorry if I mention things that aren’t even possible to do or confuse things that have nothing to do with each other.

**1. More control over fog types**
In version 0.6.5 of Sodium Extra, I could disable the environment fog added in 1.21.6 by enabling Multi-Dimension Fog and matching the fog distance to my render distance for the Overworld which completely removed that new environment fog while keeping the border and cloud fogs.

Now in 0.6.6, it looks like I can only disable whole categories (e.g., all “Atmospheric Fog”), which removes everything: border fog, cloud fog, environment fog even though I only want to remove one. It’d be really helpful to have a way to toggle fog types within each category.

**2. Percentage-based fog distance feels less Intuitive**
I noticed that fog distances are now controlled entirely by start and end multipliers instead of fixed chunk values. This means the fog start and end distances are expressed as a percentage of the current render distance rather than an absolute chunk count.

Even though it probably offer more flexibility technically, it feels less intuitive to me as a casual player. For example, I used to simply set my Nether fog to match my render distance (24 chunks) and know exactly where the fog would start. Now, with multiplier sliders that can go beyond 100% (up to 300%), it’s harder to know what percentage corresponds to a specific chunk value without doing math or guessing.

That said, I get it that for fluid fogs, using chunk counts wouldn’t make sense, so maybe a hybrid system could work: chunk-based controls for dimension fogs, and multiplier or block-based controls for fluid fogs? Or maybe make it a setting apart?

**3. Nether, End, Boss fogs merged?**
I also noticed that the Nether fog settings seem to be merged together with the End and boss fogs in the same control group. Does this mean I can no longer adjust the Nether fog distance independently from the End dimension’s fog or the fog effects during the boss fight? For example, if I want a different fog distance in the Nether than what appears in the End or during the Dragon fight, it seems impossible now.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Optional switch of "cutout" render type for "cutout_mipped" (optifine feature)
issues.body:
This feature was recently rejected from Sodium: https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium/issues/2846

It's been a part of optifine since a while ago.

TLDR: Vanilla disables mipmapping for a lot of cutout blocks, which causes atrocious aliasing.
![2024-10-18_15 54 38](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85cf4e94-c397-49bc-ac55-c438f3e06748)

Optifine remedies this and automatically switches blocks using "cutout" render type for "cutout_mipped".
 
Since there is no maintained standalone mod to add this behaviour to sodium I think sodium extra should add it, considering the description says "Sodium Extra aims to bring most of OptiFine's eye-candy options to Sodium" (and fixing this eyesore would definitely count as eye-candy)

There is a handful of exceptions that do need to use "cutout" render type. That being glass, redstone wire and chains, because these blocks melt away into nothing with mips. Those should be forced to keep using the "cutout" render type, either via hardcoding those block ID's (what optifine does) or putting them into a config file. The latter would be preferred, as it'd allow users to exclude any modded blocks which might run into issues when mipmapping is forced on.


Personally I think this should be on by default, (like in optifine) but that's up to you.

issues.title: Feature request: cyclindrical fog
issues.body:
In some recent-ish versions of Minecraft (1.18?), the fog has been modified from cylindrical to spherical. In some even more recent versions of Sodium (0.5?), it has been updated to match vanilla behavior. That causes the world to stop rendering when flying over at high altitude, because the world is culled behind the spherical fog. 

Some people prefered the cylindrical fog (and related, the cylindrical fog culling), but at the moment there is no great option to enable cylindrical fog with Sodium (sodium-extra can disable the fog entirely, and that works properly with sodium fog culling, but that also disable distance fog, not only vertical fog). 

Related to https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/issues/2026, which I think is an overreach for base Sodium, but is on topic for Sodium-extra.

0.5.11

### What happened?

When enabling one of the options, either Show FPS or Show Coordinates, it breaks rendering the color sliders background in my mod CList. For the custom gradient rendering on them, I use [vertexes](https://github.com/PouekDEV/CList/blob/1.21/src/main/java/one/pouekdev/coordinatelist/CListWaypointConfig.java#L138).

issues.title: [Feature request] fsr 1.0 implemenattion
issues.body:
**HI**, I was wondering if you would be interested in implementing **FSR 1.0 into Sodium Extras**. This would be beneficial because it would allow players with really bad PCs (like me) to play on a lower resolution (for performance) without the quality impacts of no upscaling.

---

**Background**
I have done lots of Reasearch on fsr improvements and I think it would really help players with ultra-low end pc's like me. Also it has been ported to opengl so it should be easy to include without a lot of extra work converting the glsl to opengl from vulkan.

**Impact on players**:
Imagine the frustration of a player with an outdated PC—struggling to run their favorite game smoothly. They face lag, stuttering, and pixelated visuals. FSR 1.0 changes that narrative. It evokes feelings of relief and excitement as players witness smoother gameplay, even on low-end systems. No more compromises between performance and visual quality.

**Details**
Let's delve into the technical details. FSR 1.0 employs advanced upscaling algorithms that dynamically enhance lower-resolution textures without sacrificing image quality. By intelligently interpolating pixels, it maintains sharpness while significantly boosting frame rates. The result? A win-win situation for both players and developers—better performance without compromising visual fidelity.

---

By incorporating FSR 1.0 into Sodium Extras, we empower players to enjoy their favorite games on older hardware, fostering inclusivity and expanding our player base. Let's make gaming accessible for everyone!

---

issues.title: Support for MacBook displays with a notch
issues.body:
Hi! I've been using Sodium Extra for a few years and I love it! I especially love the "reduce resolution on macOS" feature as it allows me to play the game with the native fullscreen mode of macOS instead of the regular Minecraft one, which is really buggy.

There's something a bit frustrating though when I'm playing on my laptop's display (MBP 14). I'm effectively playing in 1512 x 945px (half of 3024 x 1890) which isn't really "full screen" as it's missing the top part of the screen, where the notch is. The true resolution of that display is 3024 x 1964 including the notch area, which means the ideal halved full screen resolution should be 1512 x 982px.

The same logic applies to the other recent Mac laptops (MBP 16 and MBA M2), you have the regular 16:10 aspect ratio + the notch area as a bonus.

![e7gbkmfp4bu71](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/50768582/7abd820f-321f-4165-bd72-e57a3424551a)

I know it sounds a little convoluted but having that additional row of pixels makes it way more immersive. This is how I usually play (macOS native full screen, reduce resolution toggled, 1512 x 945px): 

![IMAGE 2023-11-15 20:12:35](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/50768582/5984be90-b8cd-4bb3-8581-289153c01c03)

And this is what it would look like in the correct aspect ratio (achieved through Minecraft's normal full screen mode, 3024 x 1964px):

![IMAGE 2023-11-15 20:12:31](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/50768582/882033dc-1bda-45a2-957a-fcb6eb4187a3)

Would really love it if Sodium Extra could support it properly! Thank you 😊

issues.title: Max fog distance incompatibility with Nvidium mod, causing blacked out terrain
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [X] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Minecraft version.

1.20.2

### Sodium Extra version.

0.5.2

### Sodium version.

0.5.3

### What happened?

<sub>*[Nvidium 0.2.0](https://modrinth.com/mod/nvidium) is a Sodium rendering engine used to greatly increase performance on systems with certain NVIDIA graphics cards.*</sub>

Pretty much the title. Setting the max fog distance to the maximum (so, disabling fog) causes faraway terrain *that'd otherwise be hidden by fog* to fade out to all black. Other mods [(example)](https://modrinth.com/mod/bactromod) that disable fog don't seem to cause this problem.

### Examples:
*The vanilla fog in the Nether is thicker by design (and slightly different to the Overworld's), leading to this. Note how entities that technically are within my render distance are rendered properly.*
![](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/106876032/2342dd12-da2e-4116-8257-6b41545018d8)

*Fresh instance with just Nvidium, Sodium and Sodium Extra (meaning there are no other incompatibilities). Notice the black terrain.*
![2023-10-14_09 34 37](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/106876032/7483575b-ba48-4b6a-aa9e-0a98b3cb2ae8)

*Same world/instance, but fog distance reverted to default. The terrain that was previously black is now completely hidden by the fog.*
![](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/assets/106876032/9a18665e-7145-4b37-8391-ceb9a5690030)



### Relevant log.

No log is required to observe the issue

### Additional information.

My best assumption is that the method Sodium Extra uses to change fog distance does not integrate well with alternative rendering engines, and rather focuses on *just* Sodium's default rendering. I think it should be changed, seeing how alternative mods can already change fog regardless of rendering engine, and how Sodium Extra is considered the go-to and most popular option for disabling fog on Fabric.

issues.title: [Bug] Beacon beam rendering optimizations breaks when using Iris shaders
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [X] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my crash.

### Minecraft version.

1.20.1

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.21

### Sodium version.

0.4.10

### What happened?

After updating to Sodium Extra 0.4.21, the game freezes just after loading my world. In most cases I then have to kill the process but it sometimes crashes to desktop instead. Got the following error but not every time:

```
The game crashed whilst rendering block entity
Error: java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Source format has fewer elements than destination format
```

Version 0.4.20 works fine. Adding crash report and latest.log related to the error above.

issues.title: Extreme GPU load when using Xaeros World Map with High Zoom Value + Sodium + Sodium Extra
issues.body:
What happens
When one opens Xaeros World Map and uses a Zoom Level of > 1.00 the load on my GPU drastically increases. Power Consumption goes from 50W to over 200W, Clock goes from 500MHz to over 3000MHz, Load is nearly 100%. The higher the zoom value, the more the load increases.
As soon, as i close the map (ESC) the load goes back to normal.

Why do i write this here
This ONLY happens, when i am using sodium in combination with sodium extra. Using sodium only does not result in such a behavior.

Versions:
-     Minecraft 1.19.4
-     fabric-loader-0.14.19-1.19.4
-     fabric-api-0.76.0+1.19.4

issues.title: NPE related to fog when attempting to join any world.
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [x] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my crash.

### Minecraft version.

1.19.2

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.12

### Sodium version.

0.4.4

### What happened?

When I attempt to join either a single-player world, or a multi-player world, the game crashes with an NPE with what appears to be a relation to fog. I'm assuming this relation based on the line `net.minecraft.class_758.handler$zlb000$applyFog(class_758.java:1028)` in the crash reports attached below.

I've verified it is Sodium Extra, by launching the game with only Sodium, Fabric API, and this mod. Removing/disabling Sodium Extra allows me to join worlds without issues. Also, downgrading to Sodium Extra 0.4.11 allows me to join worlds; something in the 0.4.12 update is what appears to be the issue.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Fog falloff
issues.body:
Can you add a fog falloff slider? It would control the distance (in percentage) where the fog starts rendering, like [Custom Fog](https://modrinth.com/mod/custom-fog), or more recently, [Simple Fog Control](https://modrinth.com/mod/simplefog).

Differently from these mods though, I'd suggest to only feature the `fog start` parameter, to make it simpler and easier for users, as these mods can get a little overkill with customizability

issues.title: Game fails to load when using prime-run wrapper command
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [X] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Minecraft version.

1.18.2

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.4

### Sodium version.

0.4.1

### What happened?

When trying to use `prime-run` as a wrapper command in MultiMC to use my dedicated GPU (NVIDIA RTX 3070 Max-Q) with Sodium 0.4.1 and Sodium Extra 0.4.4, the game fails to load and exits with:

`X Error of failed request:  BadValue (integer parameter out of range for operation)`
`  Major opcode of failed request:  150 (GLX)`
`  Minor opcode of failed request:  16 (X_GLXVendorPrivate)`
`  Value in failed request:  0xffffffffffffffff`
`  Serial number of failed request:  0`
`  Current serial number in output stream:  181`
`Process exited with code 1.`

Note: this isn't shown in the attached log, but appears in the console directly after what's shown in the log after the game fails to load.

I first encountered this problem when trying to load Fabulously Optimized 3.8.2 while using `prime-run` as the wrapper command. I figured out it was Sodium Extra by getting the game to properly launch when I downgraded it to the version used in Fabulously Optimized 3.8.1 (from 0.4.4 to 0.4.3).

I also tried using `prime-run` as the wrapper command in a clean 1.18.2 Fabric instance with only Sodium 0.4.1 and Sodium Extra 0.4.4, and it still failed to load (the attached log is from this). Once again, downgrading Sodium Extra from 0.4.4 to 0.4.3 allowed the game to load properly.

### Relevant log.

https://pastebin.com/NCEqbbyR

### Additional information.

I use Arch BTW.

issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [ ] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my crash.

### Minecraft version.

1.18.1

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.0

### Sodium version.

0.4.0

### What happened?

after a while of using sodium extra with no issues. I booted up minecraft and couldnt join any servers. it would crash as soon as it attempted to load the server. then I attempted to go to video settings and it would also crash the game. so I deleted the original instance and made a new one. didnt fix it so I removed some mods one by one to find which one was broken. after a while it worked when I removed the sodium extra mod. re downloaded the mod again and same effect

### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [ ] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my crash.

1.18.2

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.3

### Sodium version.

0.4.1

issues.title: [Feature request] Toggle/Adjust Beacon Beam
issues.body:
Even with Sodium installed, the beacon beams have a significant impact on FPS. For example, in my case, 50 activated beacons reduce FPS by 27% if the beams are not colored in any color, and by 87% if 10 layers of glass are used for coloring.

I suggest adding an option to switch the visibility of the beams or a slider to adjust their height. At the moment, the beam is visible up to a height of 1080 blocks, which greatly affects FPS. In 1.16.5 and below, the maximum beam height was 256 blocks and did not have such a disastrous effect, so even a simple possibility of adjusting the beam height between these values or just disabling them would be very useful.

issues.title: Support for Emissive Textures
issues.body:
Would it be possible to add support for emissive textures, similar to OptiFine's emissive textures feature?

Specifically, I would like to be able to use this with Sodium (i.e. without OptiFine):
https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/texture-packs/emissive-ores-1-17

Minecraft 1.18.2
Latest Fabric Loader: 0.13.3
Macbook Pro Mid-2014 macOS Big Sur 11.6.5
CPU: 2.8 GHz Dual-Core Intel Core i5
GPU: Intel Iris 1536 MB
Java JDK 18 and JRE 1.8.0_321

So I've installed sodium and iris, and also put sodium extra (all these latest versions for 1.18.2). When I load only Sodium+Iris everything is fine but when I add Sodium Extra my minecraft looks like this:

ScreenShot 1: https://i.ibb.co/8xrFgmF/pic1.png
SS 2: https://i.ibb.co/KVrDzxw/pic2.png
SS 3: https://i.ibb.co/TL77vBf/pic3.png

Would be really nice if you guys could figure out what's causing this or what I'm doing wrong. Thanks in advance

issues.title: GPU Hard Crash on Linux with amdgpu drivers
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [x] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my crash.

### Minecraft version.

1.16.5

### Sodium Extra version.

0.4.2

### Sodium version.

0.2.0

### What happened?

I'm running into graphical corruption issues when running custom 1.16.5 modpack I'm putting together which cause the entire system to freeze, necessitating a hard reboot of the entire machine. I can start up the game, play for about a minute or two, then my monitor briefly loses signal, before visuals return looking like [this](https://i.imgur.com/s9eYdSa.jpeg). At this point, the system requires a hard reboot to restore functionality. I can only reproduce this with Sodium and Sodium Extras installed. I was able to switch to a different tty for the purpose of extracting a dmesg log.

### Relevant logs

[dmesg.log](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/files/8328393/dmesg.log)


### Additional information

I'm running fully updated Arch Linux with an AMD RX 580 GPU. I've observed this issue on both Wayland and X.org, with both linux and linux-lts kernels with systemd-based initramfs, and with both mesa and mesa-git packages.

I initially discovered this issue using the Forge port Magnesium Extras, however I can confirm the issue is also present under Sodium Extras.

Alternatively, there may be a warning prompt before activation and moving such settings to one separate (maybe even collapsible?) group.

issues.title: Sodium Extra messes up GUI scale, makes everything looks pixelated.
issues.body:
### Make sure you are not opening a duplicate.

- [x] [I have searched the issue tracker](https://github.com/FlashyReese/sodium-extra-fabric/issues?q=) and did not find an issue describing my bug.

### Minecraft version.

1.18.1

### Sodium Extra version.

0.3.9

### Sodium version.

0.4.0-alpha6+build.14

### What happened?

After Installing the mod, you notice that your GUI scale gets messed up, you fix it, then you realise that the sizes changed, so you just mess around with it until you get something that matches you last GUI Scale. Opening the settings in sodium you see all the new features, now if you join Singleplayer/Multiplayer. You notice your world looks pixelated like some low-quality image. I removed the mod and restarted minecraft and then everything came back normally. 

**Im on macOS and most issues seemed to match mine but never said my issue.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Disable OpenGL debug messages
issues.body:
There a many configurations with resource packs, shaders, mods and hardware where one or more debug messages are logged every frame. 
That's why I suggest an option to disable debug logging. An optimal solution would be some kind of error aggregation UI / Toast / Chat Message. 

Technical note:
The debug callback is registered in `net.minecraft.client.gl.GlDebug`.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Add planar fog toggle
issues.body: Could you add a toggle for planar fog? It helps in improving visibility in areas like the Nether without completely removing the fog. I have seen this option in MrMangoHands' fork of Sodium and thought that it would fit nicely into this mod.

issues.title: Allow the debug screen to refresh slower?
issues.body:
When using OptiFine or canvas renderer (with **Steady Debug Screen** switch enabled); the debug screen becomes slow at refreshing debug screen which allows accuracy to be improved and allows FPS to be kept stable without having to refresh every frame.

Sodium on the other hand completely lacks this as it relays on the every-frame-refresh method instead which vanilla has, meaning accuracy is decreased [as discussed in one of the mods here](https://github.com/juliand665/Dynamic-FPS/issues/46) and can also sometimes decrease FPS entirely in specific machine units.

issues.title: Incompatiblity with Mine Little Pony
issues.body:
In this case Mine Little Pony, but can also affect anything else that extends ArmorStandEntityRenderer. The problem is because you're introducing an override of a generic method in your mixin.

To illustrate, my code would look like this:
```
public class PonyStandRenderer extends ArmorStandEntityRenderer {
    @Override
    public void render(ArmorStandEntity entity, float entityYaw, float tickDelta, MatrixStack stack, VertexConsumerProvider renderContext, int lightUv) {
        this.model = isPonita(entity) ? pony : human;
        super.render((Object)entity, entityYaw, tickDelta, stack, renderContext, lightUv);
    }
    <extra stuff omitted>
}
```

Whilst ArmorStandEntityRender would look like this (after applying Mixins)
```
public class ArmorStandEntityRenderer extends LivingEntityRenderer {

    @Override
    public /*bridge*/ void render(Object entity, float f, float g, MatrixStack matrices, VertexConsumerProvider vertexConsumers, int light) {
         this.render((ArmorStandEntity)entity, f, g, matrices, vertexConsumers, light);
    }
    public void render(ArmorStandEntity entity, float f, float g, MatrixStack matrices, VertexConsumerProvider vertexConsumers, int light) {
        if (SodiumExtraClientMod.options().renderSettings.armorStand) {
            super.render((Object)entity, f, g, matrices, vertexConsumers, light);
        } else {
            if (this.hasLabel(entity)) {
                this.renderLabelIfPresent(entity, entity.getDisplayName(), matrices, vertexConsumers, light);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

I've added casts in to make it clear what's happening here. I believe because Java is adding that bridge method in, my super call is going to the bridge method, which is then looping back up, so you end up with something like this:
- ArmorStandEntityRenderer.render(Object, ...)
- PonyStandRenderer.render(ArmorStandEntity, ...)
- ArmorStandEntityRenderer.render(Object, ...)
- etc... to stack overflow

The fix for this would be to avoid using @Override in your Mixins. So replace the ArmorStandEntityRendererMixin with one like this:

```
@Mixin(LivingEntityRenderer.class)
abstract class LivingEntityRendererMixin<T extends LivingEntity, M extends EntityModel<T>> extends EntityRenderer<T> implements FeatureRendererContext<T, M> {
    LivingEntityRendererMixin() {super(null, null, 0);}

    @Inject(method = "render", at = @At("HEAD"), cancellable = true)
    private void onRender(T entity, float f, float g, MatrixStack matrices, VertexConsumerProvider vertexConsumers, int light, CallbackInfoReturnable cbi) {
        if (entity instanceof ArmorStandEntity && !SodiumExtraClientMod.options().renderSettings.armorStand) {
            cbi.cancel();
            if (this.hasLabel(entity)) {
                this.renderLabelIfPresent(entity, entity.getDisplayName(), matrices, vertexConsumers, light);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

issues.title: Implement Mixin Configuration Plugin
issues.body: The project currently lacks a configuration system for mixins. By implementing it, it should allow the user to disable conflicting mixins(#92 features in this case) with other mods, thus improving compatibility. This also allows the user to disable unwanted features.

issues.title: [Feature Request] Separate camera/hand bobbing, sprint indication
issues.body:
Hi. First off, I appreciate your work on this mod and it's very nice to use.
In Minecraft you can disable dynamic FOV which is nice for people who get motion sick like me. A consequence of this is that it's very hard to know when you're sprinting and when you aren't. 
I came to the idea of combining a feature in Sk1er's Patcher mod in which camera movement/bobbing is disabled, but the hand bobbing is kept, **but in this implementation only when sprinting!**
In effect, static FOV, no hand bobbing when walking/idling, but when you sprint your hand bobs. 
This also would add the feature of separate toggles for camera & hand bobbing, but also with a toggle for "only when sprinting".
tl;dr separate options to disable camera & hand/viewmodel bobbing, option under to enable viewmodel bobbing only while sprinting which serves as a sprint indication.

issues.title: "Circular Render Distance" Toggle Option
issues.body:
A toggle for a "circular render distance" is something that might be really nice. Because, this is a feature that I, and many others, might find useful.

Since a visual explanation is probably best, here's what would be rendered for a render distance of 6 chunks:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46940694/124668671-310bc580-de7f-11eb-8d78-3f04712ec7cb.png)
### Key:
- Red Dot: Where the player is standing.
- Red Circle: A circle with a radius of 6 chunks.
- Green Line: a 6 chunk long line.
- Blue Square: Chunks that are rendered.
- Yellow Square: Chunk that *would have* been rendered, according to vanilla behaviour, but are *not* rendered with "circular render distance".
- White Square: Chunk that isn't rendered.


Basically, chunks would be rendered in a circle instead of in a square around the player. This would allow players to increase their render distance slightly, because it wouldn't render the corner chunks which are further from the player.
